page: Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-amd is a High Performance family virtual server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The hardware profile is completed by 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core, and 60 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core compute capabilities and memory-bound operations. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 10%. However, multi-core performance drops to average levels, and Passmark CPU tests for physics, encryption, and extended instructions register in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a primary bottleneck; the Passmark memory score and database operations fall into the bottom 10%, while cached small-block read bandwidth is weak at 280.84 GB/sec. Large-block read and write memory bandwidths remain average.

Given the shared CPU allocation and constrained 2.0 GB memory capacity, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that require bursty single-threaded compute but have low memory footprints. It is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, and simple automation scripts. It is poorly suited for database-heavy applications, high-throughput static web serving, or memory-intensive operations, as evidenced by its low Passmark database score and weak Redis SET throughput.
